findings.description: storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, meaning data at rest in the RDS instance (and any snapshots) is not encrypted, violating encryption-at-rest requirements for sensitive data such as employee records.

publicly_accessible is set to true, exposing the MySQL database instance directly to the internet rather than restricting it to the private VPC network, dramatically increasing attack surface for a data store holding credentials and application data.

The database uses a hard-coded default master username ('admin') and a password sourced from var.password with no indication of secrets-manager integration; this same password value is later interpolated in plaintext into EC2 user data, increasing the exposure surface of the credential across state files and instance metadata.

The EC2 user_data script embeds the database username and password (var.password) in cleartext when writing /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. user_data is stored in the instance metadata service and in Terraform state, making it readable by anyone with API/console access to the instance or state, or with access to the metadata service.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource '*' to the EC2 instance role, violating least privilege. Because this role is attached to an EC2 instance that is likely reachable from the public internet (via a security group not shown to restrict ingress) and embeds DB credentials, a compromise of the instance would grant near-total control over S3, EC2, and RDS resources in the account.

The security group egress rule allows all protocols and all ports to 0.0.0.0/0 for the RDS-associated security group, removing any network egress restriction and increasing risk of data exfiltration if the database is compromised.
The database uses the well-known default master username 'admin', which combined with public accessibility increases the risk of successful credential-guessing or brute-force attacks.
